review_method: For each monster()/areamonster() call previously indexed as an 'approximate instance-template association' (map_template_approximate=true in bestiary.v1.json, meaning the base exporter's unscoped nearest-preceding-assignment-within-1000-characters heuristic), re-derived the call's enclosing NPC-script label body (Hercules script labels reached via donpcevent/settimer/OnTouch each start a fresh script execution scope per doc/script_commands.txt's '.@' scope-variable description) and located every '.@map$ = instance_mapname("TEMPLATE");' assignment within that same label body preceding the call. All 376 originally-approximate associations across 43 distinct (file, label, template) groups had exactly one same-scope preceding assignment, matching the original heuristic's guessed template in every case -- so this pass confirms rather than corrects those 376, but on a control-flow basis (same execution scope) instead of an unscoped proximity guess. No genuinely-unresolvable case was found in this batch; a stricter search (requiring the assignment to be in the literal same label, not merely within 1000 characters regardless of label boundaries) did not surface any group lacking a same-scope assignment. This does not resolve calls to a literal concrete map: instance_mapname() templates are bound to a dynamically-created per-instance map at runtime, which static source review cannot observe -- see each entry's note.
